title: Step 2 - Max Pooling in CNNs: Enhancing Spatial Invariance for Image Recognition

cues.en: -: Hello and welcome back to the course on Deep Learning.
cues.zh: 大家好，歡迎回到深度學習課程。

cues.en: Today we're talking about max pooling and we've got some very exciting slides coming up ahead and even a special surprise at the very end of the tutorial.
cues.zh: 今天談最大池化。接下來有很精彩的投影片，教學最後還有特別驚喜。

cues.en: So let's get started.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: The first question is, what is pooling and why do we need it?
cues.zh: 首先，什麼是池化？為什麼需要它？

cues.en: Well, to answer that question let's have a look at these images.
cues.zh: 要回答這個問題，先看這幾張影像。

cues.en: On these three images, we've got a cheetah.
cues.zh: 三張影像裡都有一隻獵豹。

cues.en: In fact, it is the same exact cheetah.
cues.zh: 其實是完全相同的那隻獵豹。

cues.en: On the first image, the image is positioned properly and the cheetah is looking straight at you.
cues.zh: 第一張正常擺正，獵豹正看著你。

cues.en: On the second image, it's a bit rotated, and the third image it's a bit squashed.
cues.zh: 第二張稍微旋轉，第三張則被壓扁了一些。

cues.en: And the thing here is that we want the neural network to be able to recognize the cheetah in every single one of these images.
cues.zh: 我們希望神經網路在每張影像中，都能辨識出獵豹。

cues.en: In fact, this is just one cheetah.
cues.zh: 而這還只是一隻獵豹。

cues.en: What if we have lots of different cheetahs?
cues.zh: 如果有很多不同獵豹呢？

cues.en: Here's a cheetah, here's a cheetah, here's another cheetah, here's a cheetah, here's a cheetah, and here's a cheetah.
cues.zh: 這是一隻、這是一隻，這裡又一隻，這裡一隻、這裡一隻，這裡也是。

cues.en: And we want the neural network to recognize all of these cheetahs as cheetahs and how can it do that if they're all looking in different directions,
cues.zh: 我們希望神經網路都能把牠們辨識為獵豹，但牠們朝向不同方向，

cues.en: they're all in different parts of the image.
cues.zh: 也在影像的不同位置，該怎麼辦？

cues.en: They're like, their faces are positioned in different parts of the image.
cues.zh: 牠們的臉位於影像不同部位。

cues.en: Somebody's on the right hand side, somebody's on the left corner, somebody's in the middle.
cues.zh: 有些在右側、有些在左邊角落、有些在中央。

cues.en: They're all a bit different.
cues.zh: 每隻都有點不同。

cues.en: The texture's a little bit different.
cues.zh: 紋理略有不同，

cues.en: The lighting is a bit different.
cues.zh: 光線也略有不同。

cues.en: There's lots of little differences.
cues.zh: 有許多細微差異。

cues.en: And so if the neural network looks for exactly a certain feature, for instance, a distinctive feature of the cheetah is the tears that are
cues.zh: 假設神經網路尋找某個精確特徵，例如獵豹的顯著特徵，就是

cues.en: on its face going from the eyes or the sh-, shadows that look like tears.
cues.zh: 臉上從眼睛往下延伸、像淚痕的陰影。

cues.en: The texture, the pattern that is going from its eyes down its, on the sides of its nose.
cues.zh: 也就是從眼睛向下、沿著鼻子兩側的紋理與圖案。

cues.en: It looks like tears.
cues.zh: 看起來像淚痕。

cues.en: That's a distinctive feature of the cheetah.
cues.zh: 這是獵豹的明顯特徵。

cues.en: But if it's looking for that feature, which it learned from certain cheetahs in an exact location or an exact shape
cues.zh: 但如果它只尋找從某些獵豹學到、出現在固定位置，且有特定形狀、

cues.en: or form or texture, it'll never find these other cheetahs.
cues.zh: 形式或紋理的特徵，就永遠找不到其他獵豹。

cues.en: So we have to make sure that our neural network has a property called spacial invariance, meaning that it doesn't care
cues.zh: 因此必須讓神經網路具有空間不變性，也就是它不在意

cues.en: where the features are allocated.
cues.zh: 特徵位於哪裡。

cues.en: Not, not so much as in which part of the image, because we, we've kind of taken that into consideration with our map, with our pool, with our convolution layer.
cues.zh: 這裡不主要是指影像的哪個部位，因為特徵圖、卷積層已多少考量了這點。

cues.en: But it doesn't have to care if the features are a bit tilted, if the features are a bit different in texture, if the features are a bit closer, or if features are a bit further apart,
cues.zh: 而是即使特徵稍微傾斜、紋理略有不同、彼此稍微靠近或遠離，

cues.en: relative to, relative to each other.
cues.zh: 也不應受到太大影響。

cues.en: So if the feature itself is a bit distorted, our neural network has to have some level of flexibility to be able to still find that feature.
cues.zh: 特徵本身稍微變形時，神經網路必須有一定彈性，仍能找到該特徵。

cues.en: And that is what pooling is all about.
cues.zh: 這就是池化的作用。

cues.en: So let's have a look at how pooling works.
cues.zh: 來看看池化如何運作。

cues.en: Here's our feature map.
cues.zh: 這是特徵圖。

cues.en: So we've already done our convolution, and we've completed that part.
cues.zh: 卷積已經做完，那個部分已完成。

cues.en: And now we we're working with the convolution layer.
cues.zh: 現在處理的是卷積層。

cues.en: Now we're going to apply pooling.
cues.zh: 接著要套用池化。

cues.en: So how does it work?
cues.zh: 怎麼做呢？

cues.en: We're gonna be applying max pooling.
cues.zh: 我們使用最大池化。

cues.en: There's several different types of pooling can apply, as mean pooling, max pooling, sum pooling, and we'll comment on those towards the end of this tutorial.
cues.zh: 池化有好幾種，包括平均池化、最大池化、加總池化，教學結尾會再說明。

cues.en: But for now, we're just applying max pooling.
cues.zh: 目前先用最大池化。

cues.en: So we take a box of 2X2 pixels like that.
cues.zh: 取一個這樣的 2 × 2 像素方框。

cues.en: And again, it doesn't have to be 2X2.
cues.zh: 同樣地，不一定非得是 2 × 2。

cues.en: You can choose any size of box.
cues.zh: 可以選擇其他大小。

cues.en: And again, we'll comment on that towards the end of the tutorial.
cues.zh: 教學結尾也會再談這點。

cues.en: And you place it in the top left hand corner, and you find the maximum value in that box.
cues.zh: 把它放在左上角，找出框內最大值。

cues.en: And then you record only that value, and you disregard the other three.
cues.zh: 只記錄這個值，忽略其他三個。

cues.en: So in your box you have four values.
cues.zh: 框裡共有四個值。

cues.en: You just disregard three, you only keep one, the maximum, which is one in this case.
cues.zh: 忽略其中三個，只保留最大值，這裡就是 1。

cues.en: Then you move your box to the right by a stride.
cues.zh: 接著向右移動一個步幅。

cues.en: You select the stride once again.
cues.zh: 步幅同樣由你選擇。

cues.en: So here we select a stride of two, and you, that's what you normally select.
cues.zh: 這裡選 2，也是通常使用的值。

cues.en: You can select the stride of one, you can select, so they're overlapping boxes.
cues.zh: 也可以選 1，那樣方框就會重疊。

cues.en: You can select any kind of stride that you like, even three if you want.
cues.zh: 想用其他步幅也行，甚至可以選 3。

cues.en: But we're selecting a stride of two here, and that's what is commonly used.
cues.zh: 這裡選常見的步幅 2。

cues.en: And then you repeat, repeat the process, you record the maximum.
cues.zh: 接著重複流程，記錄最大值。

cues.en: Here, if you cross over and doesn't matter, you just keep continue doing what you're doing.
cues.zh: 這裡超出邊界也沒關係，照樣繼續。

cues.en: So, you still record the maximum here, zero.
cues.zh: 這裡仍記錄最大值 0。

cues.en: Here, the maximum is four.
cues.zh: 這裡最大值是 4，

cues.en: Here, the maximum is two.
cues.zh: 這裡最大值是 2。

cues.en: Here are the maximum is 1, 0, 1, 02, and then 1.
cues.zh: 這裡依序是 1、0、1、0、2，再來是 1。

cues.en: So, as you can see, a few things happened.
cues.zh: 可以看到，發生了幾件事。

cues.en: First of all, we still were able to preserve the features, right?
cues.zh: 首先，仍然保留了特徵。

cues.en: The maximum numbers, they represent, because we know how the convolution layer works.
cues.zh: 我們知道卷積層如何運作，所以知道這些最大值代表什麼。

cues.en: We know that the maximum or the bit large numbers in your feature map, they represent where you actually found the closest similarity to a feature.
cues.zh: 特徵圖裡的最大值或較大數值，代表在該處找到與特徵最相似的部分。

cues.en: But by then pooling these features, we are, first of all, getting rid of 75% of the information that is not the feature,
cues.zh: 對這些特徵做池化，首先就去除了 75% 並非該特徵的資訊，

cues.en: which is, which is not the important things that we're looking out for because we are disregarding three pixels out of four.
cues.zh: 那些不是我們要找的重要內容，因為每四個像素就忽略三個。

cues.en: So we're only keeping 25%.
cues.zh: 只保留 25%。

cues.en: And then also, because we are taking the maximum of the pixels that we, or the values that we have,
cues.zh: 另外，由於取的是這些像素或數值中的最大值，

cues.en: we are, therefore, accounting for any distortion.
cues.zh: 因此也能容許變形。

cues.en: So for instance, two images in which, for example, the cheetah's tears on the eyes are in one image, they're a bit to the left or a bit rotated to the left.
cues.zh: 例如有兩張影像，其中一張的獵豹眼睛下方淚痕，稍微偏左或向左旋轉。

cues.en: And in the other one they're a bit, and they're how they're supposed to be or how we, like if we take one as the basis and then the other one, they're a bit rotated to the left.
cues.zh: 另一張則是原本的樣子。也就是把一張當作基準，另一張的特徵稍微向左旋轉。

cues.en: The, the pooled feature will be exactly the same.
cues.zh: 池化後的特徵會完全相同。

cues.en: So you can see here, if we are talking about the cheetah's tears, then let's say this is the four and this is where it was here.
cues.zh: 假設淚痕對應這個 4，它原本在這個位置。

cues.en: Then if it was a bit rotated, so for instance the four ended up over here, then when we are doing the pooling, we're still gonna get the same pooled feature map.
cues.zh: 如果稍微旋轉，4 變成出現在這裡，池化後仍會得到相同特徵圖。

cues.en: And that, that's kind of the, the principle behind it.
cues.zh: 這就是背後的原理。

cues.en: It's a very rough explanation, again, intuitive explanation, but that's the point of pooling that we're still being able to preserve the features and moreover account
cues.zh: 同樣只是粗略、直覺的解釋，但池化的重點，就是仍能保留特徵，並容許

cues.en: for their possible spatial or textural or other kind of distortions.
cues.zh: 特徵在空間、紋理或其他方面可能出現的變形。

cues.en: And in addition to all of that, we are reducing the size.
cues.zh: 除此之外，也縮小了尺寸。

cues.en: So there's another benefit.
cues.zh: 這是另一個好處。

cues.en: So we've got, we are preserving the features, we're introducing spatial invariance, we're reducing the size by 75%, which is huge,
cues.zh: 我們保留特徵、引入空間不變性，還把尺寸減少了 75%，這是很大的縮減，

cues.en: which is really gonna help us in terms of processing.
cues.zh: 對後續處理非常有幫助。

cues.en: And moreover, another benefit of pooling is we are reducing the number of parameters.
cues.zh: 池化還有一個好處，就是減少參數數量。

cues.en: So we're reducing again, by 75%, we're reducing number of parameters that are going to go into our final layers of the neural network, and, therefore, we're preventing overfitting.
cues.zh: 進入神經網路最後幾層的參數數量也減少 75%，因此能防止過度擬合。

cues.en: It is a very important benefit of pooling that we are removing information.
cues.zh: 移除資訊是池化非常重要的優點。

cues.en: And that is a good thing.
cues.zh: 而且這是好事。

cues.en: That is a good thing because that way our model won't be able to overfit onto that information because, especially, because that information is not relevant.
cues.zh: 因為這樣模型就無法對那些資訊過度擬合，尤其那些資訊本來就不重要。

cues.en: Remember, like at the very start, we were talking about even for human, us as humans, it's important to see exactly the features rather than all this other noise that is coming into our eyes.
cues.zh: 記得開頭說過，即使對人類來說，重點也是看到特徵，而不是進入眼睛的其他雜訊。

cues.en: Well, same thing for neural networks.
cues.zh: 神經網路也是如此。

cues.en: They, by disregarding the unnecessary, non-important information we're helping with preventing of overfitting.
cues.zh: 忽略不必要、不重要的資訊，有助於防止過度擬合。

cues.en: So there we go.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: That is what pooling is about.
cues.zh: 這就是池化。

cues.en: And the question here is, of course, why, why max pooling, right?
cues.zh: 接著當然會問，為什麼選最大池化？

cues.en: There's lots of different types of pooling and you know why, why a stride of two, why a size of 2X2 pixels?
cues.zh: 池化有很多種，為什麼步幅是 2？方框大小為什麼是 2 × 2 像素？

cues.en: Lots of all these things.
cues.zh: 還有許多這類問題。

cues.en: And on that note, I'd like to introduce you to this lovely research paper called "Evaluation of Pooling Operations in Convolution Architectures for Object Recognition"
cues.zh: 因此想介紹這篇很棒的研究論文 Evaluation of Pooling Operations in Convolutional Architectures for Object Recognition，

cues.en: by Dominic Sharer from University of Bon.
cues.zh: 作者是波昂大學的 Dominic Sharer。

cues.en: There's the link.
cues.zh: 這是連結。

cues.en: And the beauty about this paper is that it's very, very simple, very straightforward.
cues.zh: 這篇論文的優點是非常簡單、直接。

cues.en: So if you've never read a research paper before, which you'd like to give it a go, this is a great place to start.
cues.zh: 如果從沒讀過研究論文，但想試試，這是很好的起點。

cues.en: It's very short, only 10 pages, very easy to read.
cues.zh: 篇幅很短，只有 10 頁，非常好讀。

cues.en: And plus, the extra benefit is that now that we've discussed convolution and pooling you will be totally comfortable with everything that they're talking about in this paper.
cues.zh: 而且我們已經談過卷積與池化，所以你能輕鬆理解其中的內容。

cues.en: And you, this is a great way to actually reinforce your knowledge.
cues.zh: 這也是強化所學的好方法。

cues.en: So I highly recommend checking this paper out.
cues.zh: 因此非常推薦你讀讀。

cues.en: I'll take 20 minutes to read it and you can even skip part two which is called "Related Work," if it feels a bit far fetched or alienating, just don't read that part.
cues.zh: 大概花 20 分鐘就能讀完。如果第 2 部分 Related Work，也就是相關研究，讓你覺得太遙遠或難懂，可以跳過。

cues.en: Go straight to, from part one to part three.
cues.zh: 直接從第 1 部分讀到第 3 部分。

cues.en: And the one thing that you do need to know about this paper, they, they talk about a concept called sub-sampling.
cues.zh: 還有一件事要先知道：論文會談到 sub-sampling，次取樣這個概念。

cues.en: Well, sub-sampling is basically average pooling.
cues.zh: 次取樣基本上就是平均池化。

cues.en: So remember how, here, we were taking, we were taking the maximum, so, in our square we were taking the maximum value.
cues.zh: 剛才我們在方框裡取的是最大值。

cues.en: There's a concept called mean pooling or sum pooling.
cues.zh: 另外還有平均池化與加總池化。

cues.en: Sum pooling is you just sum these values up.
cues.zh: 加總池化就是把這些值相加。

cues.en: Average pooling or mean pooling, you take the average value out of all of these.
cues.zh: 平均池化，也就是 mean pooling，則是取這些值的平均。

cues.en: And sub-sampling is kind of like a generalization of mean pooling.
cues.zh: 次取樣可以看作平均池化的一般化版本。

cues.en: It's, it's a more kind of generalized approach to taking the average of, of these values.
cues.zh: 它是對這些數值取平均的一種更一般化做法。

cues.en: And you can read a bit more about it in the paper but otherwise just think of it as average pooling when you're reading that paper.
cues.zh: 細節可以看論文；閱讀時先把它想成平均池化就好。

cues.en: And so that's where you can get some additional information on this topic.
cues.zh: 你可以在這篇取得更多相關資訊。

cues.en: And now kind of let's recap, where have we gotten to?
cues.zh: 現在回顧一下，我們進行到哪裡？

cues.en: So there's our input image.
cues.zh: 這是輸入影像。

cues.en: Then, we applied the convolution operation, and we got the convolution layer.
cues.zh: 先套用卷積運算，得到卷積層。

cues.en: And now to each of those feature maps that we get, we've applied the pooling layer.
cues.zh: 再對每張特徵圖套用池化層。

cues.en: So we've got, we've done these two steps, convolution and pooling.
cues.zh: 所以已完成卷積和池化兩個步驟。

cues.en: And now we're going to do something very fun, something exciting.
cues.zh: 接著要做很有趣、很精彩的事情。

cues.en: We're going to experiment with this.
cues.zh: 我們來實驗看看。

cues.en: So this is a screenshot I took from a tool created by Adam Harley from, well, back when he was at Ryerson University of Computer Science.
cues.zh: 這張截圖來自 Adam Harley 製作的工具，當時他在瑞爾森大學的資訊科學系。

cues.en: And now he's at Carnegie Mellon, I think, doing his PhD and great tool.
cues.zh: 我想他現在正在卡內基美隆大學攻讀博士。這是很棒的工具。

cues.en: So let's open up, let's have a look.
cues.zh: 打開來看看。

cues.en: So, you can find it.
cues.zh: 你可以找到它。

cues.en: You, you can't actually find it through Google.
cues.zh: 不過其實用 Google 不太找得到。

cues.en: You have to know the URL.
cues.zh: 必須知道網址。

cues.en: It's S, it's just hard to find it through Google 'cause there's no text here.
cues.zh: 用 Google 比較難找，是因為這裡沒有文字。

cues.en: Sc, well just this URL, scs.ryerson.ca and then this stuff on the end.
cues.zh: 就是這個網址，scs.ryerson.ca，再加上後面這些部分。

cues.en: And basically this is exactly what we are doing but visualized.
cues.zh: 它基本上把我們正在做的事情視覺化了。

cues.en: So here you need to draw a number.
cues.zh: 你要在這裡畫一個數字。

cues.en: So let's say I draw number four, and this tool will put the number four here.
cues.zh: 例如畫個 4，工具就會把這個 4 放到這裡。

cues.en: That's your image in our first step.
cues.zh: 這就是第一步的輸入影像。

cues.en: Then this is the convolution step, right?
cues.zh: 這裡是卷積步驟，

cues.en: And this is the pooling step.
cues.zh: 這裡是池化步驟。

cues.en: And also pooling by the way is also called downsampling.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，池化也稱為下採樣。

cues.en: So pooling and downsampling are the same things.
cues.zh: 所以池化和下採樣是同一回事。

cues.en: So you can see it's applied convolution, then, it's applied pooling, and you can see how it exactly works.
cues.zh: 可以看到先套用卷積，再套用池化，也能看清楚運作方式。

cues.en: So you can see what kind of convolutions it, it has applied or what kind of filters it applied, what they look like.
cues.zh: 可以看到套用了哪些卷積、哪些濾波器，以及它們的樣子。

cues.en: You can see what features it's looking out for.
cues.zh: 也能看到它在尋找什麼特徵。

cues.en: And then it's applying pooling.
cues.zh: 接著套用池化，

cues.en: So it's reducing the size.
cues.zh: 把尺寸縮小。

cues.en: And you can see here that this is important, right?
cues.zh: 這裡有個重點。

cues.en: So you can see that this is the convolved image, and this is the pooled image.
cues.zh: 這是卷積後影像，這是池化後影像。

cues.en: And you can still see the same features.
cues.zh: 還是能看到相同特徵。

cues.en: It's just less information, but same features, right?
cues.zh: 資訊變少了，但特徵一樣。

cues.en: The features are preserved.
cues.zh: 特徵被保留下來。

cues.en: That's the important part.
cues.zh: 這才是重點。

cues.en: And moreover, if you know, if our four was a bit to the kind of like rotated a bit to the side, it would still be able to pick up very similar pooled layers.
cues.zh: 而且即使這個 4 稍微向旁邊旋轉，仍能得到很相近的池化層結果。

cues.en: And then after that, it's got more layers.
cues.zh: 後面還有更多層。

cues.en: We haven't talked about that yet.
cues.zh: 這些還沒介紹。

cues.en: So, then it's got another convolutional, convolutional layer here, which we actually won't have.
cues.zh: 它這裡又有另一個卷積層，我們的模型其實不會有這一層。

cues.en: And then it has another pooled layer, but it's basically just repeating that same process.
cues.zh: 再來又有池化層，基本上就是重複相同流程。

cues.en: And then after that, this is what we're going to be talking further down in the course.
cues.zh: 接著是課程後面會談的內容，

cues.en: It's got the fully connected layers and so on.
cues.zh: 也就是全連接層等等。

cues.en: But you can definitely play around with that.
cues.zh: 你絕對可以自己玩玩看。

cues.en: So, if I delete that you like, if I draw a seven, you'll see that it actually tells you the guess, it guesses that this is a seven
cues.zh: 如果擦掉，改畫個 7，就能看到它的猜測：它認為這是 7，

cues.en: and the second guess, the second likelihood is a three.
cues.zh: 第二個最可能的猜測則是 3。

cues.en: So you can draw it some, some challenging things, and see if it can pick them up.
cues.zh: 可以畫些比較有挑戰性的，看看它是否認得出來。

cues.en: So let's say if I draw something that looks like a zero, but it's not a finished zero, will it pick it up?
cues.zh: 例如畫一個像 0、卻沒畫完整的形狀，它認得出來嗎？

cues.en: Now this, this time, it didn't pick it up.
cues.zh: 這次沒有。

cues.en: Looks like a nine to the, to the image.
cues.zh: 對它來說，影像看起來像 9。

cues.en: What if I kind of like finish like that?
cues.zh: 如果像這樣再補一點呢？

cues.en: See now it thinks it's a zero or a nine.
cues.zh: 現在它認為是 0 或 9。

cues.en: And you can see over there what's lighting up, the zero or the nine?
cues.zh: 可以看那邊是哪個亮起來，0 還是 9？

cues.en: But we'll talk about that part further down.
cues.zh: 這部分之後會再談。

cues.en: Let's do one more.
cues.zh: 再畫一個。

cues.en: Let's say like, like eight, I, I think eights are pretty hard for this.
cues.zh: 例如 8，我覺得這個工具辨識 8 可能比較難。

cues.en: No, picked up an eight.
cues.zh: 沒有，它認出 8 了。

cues.en: So you can see that goes into an eight, and then like, after that, it stops being recognizable.
cues.zh: 可以看到這裡還看得出是 8，但後面就不再能辨認了。

cues.en: This stops making sense to us humans, right?
cues.zh: 對人類而言，這些已經看不出意義，

cues.en: These features that it's working with.
cues.zh: 也就是它正在處理的這些特徵。

cues.en: But at the same time, it is correctly recognizing that it's an eight.
cues.zh: 但它仍然能正確辨識這是 8。

cues.en: Yeah, so definitely play around with that.
cues.zh: 所以務必玩玩看。

cues.en: You can draw a smiley face, see what happens then.
cues.zh: 也可以畫個笑臉，看看會怎樣。

cues.en: Looks like a three to this, to this tool because the tool is obviously trained up only on digits from zero to nine.
cues.zh: 對這個工具來說，看起來像 3，因為它顯然只用 0 到 9 的數字訓練。

cues.en: So it, it has to recognize something there out of those, and it recognizes a three.
cues.zh: 它必須從那些類別中選一個，因此辨識成 3。

cues.en: It's like in life when you, when you see something like a, a type of fruit that you've never seen before, like a custard apple or something,
cues.zh: 就像生活中，看到從沒見過的水果，例如釋迦，

cues.en: and you think that it's like, it's a, it's a pear because you've never actually seen one before you don't know what to classify it as.
cues.zh: 可能會以為那是梨子，因為以前沒見過，不知道該歸到哪一類。

cues.en: Same thing here.
cues.zh: 這裡也是如此。

cues.en: So it, it hasn't actually trained on smiley faces, and that's why it thinks it's a three.
cues.zh: 它沒用笑臉訓練過，所以才認為是 3。

cues.en: It's the three.
So there you go.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: It's a very powerful, powerful tool.
cues.zh: 這是非常強大的工具。

cues.en: It'll be helpful for you to play around with it.
cues.zh: 親自試試會很有幫助。

cues.en: Actually you, when you put your mouse over a pixel, pixel, it'll show, it shows you where the feature detector was to pick up that pixel,
cues.zh: 把滑鼠移到像素上時，它會顯示特徵偵測器在什麼位置，才得到這個像素，

cues.en: so you can see where those, these pixels coming from.
cues.zh: 所以能看出這些像素從哪裡來。

cues.en: And also, so you can see how the filter was kind of like going through the image exactly how we did, talked about in the course.
cues.zh: 也能看到濾波器如何掃過影像，正如課程所說。

cues.en: And here you can see, you can see the, the pooling.
cues.zh: 這裡也能看到池化，

cues.en: You can see that the pooling is done with, the pooling is done with a little square size of 2X2.
cues.zh: 池化使用的是 2 × 2 小方框。

cues.en: And you can see that it's, it's a stride of two as well just as we discussed in today's tutorial.
cues.zh: 步幅同樣是 2，與今天教學介紹的一樣。

cues.en: So there you go, play, have a play around with that.
cues.zh: 就這樣，自己試玩一下吧。

cues.zh: 希望你喜歡今天的內容。

cues.zh: 期待下次與你見面。

cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你享受深度學習的樂趣。
